classification.difficultyReason: Follow explicit successive proof targets, select equal radii and triangle congruence, then combine cyclic or alternate angle facts and matching lengths; familiar scaffolded deductive chains, no unprompted new theorem.

spec.description: Circle with horizontal diameter AB through centre O. A is the left endpoint and B the right endpoint. P is on the upper-right circumference and Q on the lower-right circumference. Chords AP and AQ are drawn. ∠PAO and ∠OAQ are each labelled θ. O is marked with a red dot.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Join OP and OQ. Radii give OA=OP=OQ, so both triangles are isosceles. The given equal angles at A imply each angle at O is $180^\circ-2\theta$. Since OA is common and OP=OQ, the triangles are congruent by SAS.
By part i, matching sides in the congruent triangles AOP and AOQ give AP=AQ.

spec.description: Circle with F on the lower-left circumference, T on the upper-left circumference, S near the top and G on the upper-right circumference. Diameter FG passes through centre O. Chords FT and FS are drawn. ∠TFS and ∠SFG are each labelled θ. O is marked with a red dot.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Join OS. Since OF=OS (radii), triangle FOS is isosceles and $\angle FSO=\angle SFO$. The diagram gives $\angle SFO=\angle TFS=\theta$, so $\angle FSO=\angle TFS$.
By part iii, $\angle TFS=\angle FSO$. These are alternate angles on transversal FS, so $FT\parallel OS$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral QSPT with Q left, S upper left, P upper right and T lower right. Chords QS, SP, PT, TQ and diagonal ST are drawn. Matching double ticks identify QS = SP; matching triple ticks identify QT = PT.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: PS=QS and PT=QT are given, and ST is common. Therefore $\triangle PST\equiv\triangle QST$ (SSS).
Matching angles in the congruent triangles from part v give $\angle SPT=\angle SQT$, that is $\angle P=\angle Q$.
Q,S,P,T lie on the same circle. Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so $\angle P+\angle Q=180^\circ$.

children.label: viii
children.prompt: Prove that ST is a diameter.

answer.short: ST is a diameter by the converse of Thales.
answer.worked: Parts vi and vii give equal angles P and Q with sum $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$. Thus chord ST subtends a right angle at the circumference, so ST is a diameter by the converse of Thales.

spec.description: Two concentric circles with common centre O, marked by a red dot. A straight chord RU of the outer circle slopes upwards from left to right and intersects the inner circle at S then T. The collinear order is R, S, T, U.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: Join OS and OT. Since OS=OT (radii of the inner circle), triangle OST is isosceles, so $\angle OST=\angle OTS$.
Join OR and OU. Since OR=OU (radii of the outer circle), triangle ORU is isosceles, so $\angle ORU=\angle OUR$.
The line order is R,S,T,U. Part ix gives $\angle OTR=\angle OSU$, and part x gives $\angle ORT=\angle OUS$. Also OR=OU (outer radii). Hence $\triangle ORT\equiv\triangle OUS$ (AAS).
Matching sides from part xi give RT=US. As R,S,T,U are collinear in that order, $RS=RT-ST=US-ST=TU$.
